label: Psalm 23 (LXX 22)
title: Psalm 23 (LXX 22) The Lord Is My Shepherd
style: Warm slow Americana soul ballad, 68 BPM, gentle 6/8 sway, major key. Fingerpicked acoustic guitar and warm Hammond B3 organ, soft upright bass, light brushed drums, gentle pedal steel. Gritty gravelly male baritone, smoky and soulful but restful and unhurried, calm even in the valley. Soft gospel choir enters on the mercy bridge and stays low and warm to the end. Peaceful, tender, Sunday evening front porch.
exclude: distorted guitar, heavy drums, rock anthem, synth, EDM, autotune, belting, female lead, sad
lyrics:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
The Lord is my shepherd,
and I shall want nothing.
In a place of green grass
there he has made me dwell.
He has nourished me
by the water of rest.

[Verse 2]
He has restored my soul,
he has guided me
in the paths of righteousness
for his name's sake.

[Chorus]
Even if I should walk
in the shadow of death,
I will fear no evil,
for you are with me.
Your rod and your staff,
they have comforted me.
I will fear no evil.

[Verse 3]
You have prepared a table before me
in the presence of those who afflict me.
You have anointed my head with oil,
and your cup cheers me like the best wine.

[Chorus]
Even if I should walk
in the shadow of death,
I will fear no evil,
for you are with me.
Your rod and your staff,
they have comforted me.
I will fear no evil.

[Bridge]
Your mercy shall follow me
all the days of my life.
Your mercy shall follow me
all the days of my life.

[Final Chorus]
I will fear no evil,
for you are with me.
The Lord is my shepherd,
and I shall want nothing.

[Outro]
And I shall dwell in the house of the Lord
for a very long time.
The Lord is my shepherd.

[End]
notes: Peace and trust. Brenton Psalm 22:1 to 6 with the valley lines (22:4) as a repeated chorus. The LXX line is 'Thy mercy also shall follow me', sung as 'Your mercy shall follow me' where the choir enters. Feel reference: softer Chris Stapleton (not named in Style).

textSource.adaptation: Light singability adaptation: thou/thy to you/your, some lines split or repeated as chorus.
